subject: DataHealth POC: mutual action plan, acceptance tests and close hooks
messages:

Subject: DataHealth POC: Draft MAP & Acceptance Criteria

Hi Soojin + Ben,

Thanks again for the demo this morning. We left with a clear sense that Redwood can materially reduce inference latency on our batch scoring jobs and simplify model rollouts. Before we lock in a POC, Priya and I sketched a simple MAP so legal and procurement have something to reference. Attaching a very rough spreadsheet with timeline and owners.

High-level asks from our side:
- Validation tests for accuracy and edge-case behavior on our 3 representative datasets (ETL-v1, ETL-v2, streaming-cases)
- A service-level expectation for 95th percentile latency at the 2k token bound
- Rollback and fallback behavior if tokenization or quantization causes regressions

Can you confirm you can deliver a short acceptance test matrix (pass/fail per dataset) and a go/no-go decision gate at the end of week 4?

Attachment: DataHealth_MAP_v0.9.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Cheers,
Alex Morgan
Head of AI Engineering
DataHealth

Subject: Re: DataHealth POC: Draft MAP & Acceptance Criteria

On 2025-09-21 09:12, Alex Morgan wrote:
> Hi Soojin + Ben,
> 
> Thanks again for the demo this morning...

Alex — thanks for the clear kickoff. I reviewed the draft MAP and I think the structure is solid. I mocked a compact acceptance-test matrix and a set of exit gates that map to a single green/red decision at the end of Week 4. Sending the two artifacts below:

- Acceptance tests (CSV): per-dataset pass/fail with sample input, success metric (latency P95, concordance >= 0.92), and owner.
- Exit gates (in MAP spreadsheet): 4 checkpoints — kickoff, mid-pilot smoke, full-run validation, signoff/contracting. Each has required evidence (logs, sample outputs, replayed requests).

Key proposed acceptance criteria (short form):
1) Latency: P95 <= 450ms for 2k token batched inference across the ETL-v2 dataset (measured under our parallelism plan).
2) Quality: Concordance against your golden labels >= 0.92 (macro F1 basis) across all three datasets.
3) Regression guard: No more than 1% token-level disagreement on a 500-sample stratified holdout vs. baseline.
4) Reliability: Successful kv-cache warmup and no silent token truncations across 24-hour run.

Planned fallback behaviors (if a gate fails):
- Timebox remediation sprint (3 business days) + detailed RCA.
- If latency regressions persist, fall back to a compatible quantized variant we ship for the POC (documented in MAP).

Next steps I propose:
- Ben to own the mutual action plan updates and coordinate the acceptance-test execution window.
- Lauren to coordinate SRE/CS touchpoints and evidence collection.
- Alex/Priya to confirm the canonical datasets and share golden-labels by COB Friday.

I attached: [Attachment: acceptance_test_matrix.csv (CSV)] and included a short SOW stub in Drive (link below).

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick 20-min alignment call if useful.

—
Soojin Lee
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

Attachments referenced: acceptance_test_matrix.csv

On Sun, Sep 21, 2025 at 12:45 PM soojin_lee@redwood.com wrote:
> Alex — thanks for the clear kickoff. I reviewed the draft MAP...

Appreciate the fast turnaround, Soojin. A couple quick clarifications and additions from the RM/ops side:

Clarifying Qs:
- Measurement harness: do you want us to run the full dataset under identical hardware (same GPU class) or do you want us to run on your schedule in your environment? We can run both; suggest Redwood-run for baseline and a cross-run to verify on your infra.
- Golden-label gating: will DataHealth provide an evaluation script (preferred) or do you want Redwood to run our internal evaluation and share results for you to validate?

Suggested failure-mode runbook (added to MAP):
1) Detect: anomaly surfaced by smoke tests (latency spike > 2x expected OR concordance drop > 4 p.p.).
2) Triage: capture KV-cache stats, tokenization diffs, quantization logs.
3) Immediate mitigation: switch traffic to quantized-compatible model variant; trigger telemetry snapshot.
4) Escalation: if mitigation fails after 3 hours, executive notification and decision to pause POC.

I uploaded a lightly redlined SOW and a suggested timeline.
Attachment: SOW_draft_v1.pdf (pdf)

I'll coordinate a REPLAY window with CS to show how we collect the evidence artifacts (logs + sample outputs). Lauren — can you take ownership of the evidence checklist and call out what we need from DataHealth (formats, S3/Drive access)?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
